metadata.othernotes:
Background

- Jura is a young fighter pilot for a spacecraft. She is second-ranked in a team of pilot girls around her age (late teens/early twenties) that defend the larger vessel "Nirvana" with their smaller gunships known as "Dreads." This is the DREAD TEAM, which is only one part of the whole crew.
- The Nirvana is crewed by pirates: ~150 women, 3 male prisoners. Their captain is an old woman named Magno Vivan, hence their group's name "Magno's Family."
- The women's home planet is Mejare (meh-JEHR, メジェール), a colony settled by spacefaring Earthlings. Mejare's population is all female. Women form couples and families there, having children together with the aid of technology. Jura's biological parents (and those of all her crewmates) were, implicitly, both women.
- Mejare is at war with a neighboring colony, the all-male Tarak. After several generations of separation, each does not see the other sex as human anymore. The war itself is at something of a stalemate. Mejare has more technology and resources, but Tarak is more efficient with what it has.
- Jura has some familiarity with men due to their prisoners, who were made part of the crew---a pilot, a doctor, and a helmsman. She understands that men are human like she is and that they normally live together, but the details remain a mystery.
- Other colonies exist with other societies. Earth in this time is environmentally devastated and has been attacking colonies to harvest colonists' organs.
- Mejare is a fleet nation, having failed to properly terraform the surface for some time, to the "empire's" embarrassment. Its cities are built in ships orbiting the planet. It is unlikely that Jura has ever lived on a planet's surface for any significant amount of time.
- Jura was probably wealthy as a child, like many of her crewmates. At some indeterminate point, she was likely displaced from her living district due to energy shortages and subsequently recruited as a pirate. She does not appear to have contact with any family.
- As pirates, the crew hides out in Mejare's asteroid belts and raids both sides of the conflict for resources, mostly Tarak. An incident at the show's beginning involving their Paksis (PAKE-sis) energy core and a wormhole threw them into deep space, far from their own system, with their aforementioned male prisoners and now privy to Earth's designs for both of their homes.
- Vandread is heavily influenced by Star Trek. Meia and Jura's presence in SPNatI is explained as another Paksis warp, this one intentionally taken to experience what Earth was like in the past---a one-off away mission like you might find in Trek. (The rest of the crew is nearby, either on or above the planet.)

Personality

- Jura is beautiful and she knows it. She feels "you don't lose anything by being seen," and she loves to be admired. She's vain, self-absorbed, and carefully maintains her appearance. Wants attention for her beauty and strength (as a fighter pilot).
- Loves anything she perceives as "elegant" or powerful, including imagined scenarios.
- Liable to whine and complain when things don't go her way or as she envisioned. Has a childish way of speaking when she's lost in fantasy or too distraught to project maturity.
- Very open with her feelings, announcing interest and voicing displeasure. Heaps physical affection onto people she likes. Considers her embrace a reward unto itself.
- Not afraid to flirt or flex her looks to get what she wants.
- DOES take her job seriously, despite her high-strung attitude. Worries about cracking under pressure or failing to live up to expectations. Lacks leadership experience.
- Sensitive beneath her bluster. Often lets the more tenacious Barnette, her girlfriend, take charge in dangerous situations. Likes being protected, hates being lonely.
- Following from this, Jura is charmed by serious, steadfast, jealous types, and prefers people who are clean and pretty. Seems to prefer feminine aesthetics.
- Brought a sidearm, her sword. Has reason to doubt Earthlings' trustworthiness.
- "When I want something, I do it." Willing to insert herself into others' social lives and fix their problems, either by addressing them directly or hatching schemes. Can be quite supportive in this way.
- Wants to learn more about men. Believes becoming pregnant by a man's seed---the first Mejarian to do so---will make her famous. Sex with men is a separate but also fascinating prospect. She has not realized the connection between these things.
- Attracted to other girls, obviously. Has a reputation for taking initiative in this regard.
- Still generally wary of men until she's gotten to know them; pushy with her peers, but more respectful to those older than her.

Good Topics/Touchstones

- Men's anatomy/physiology/behavior/desires (e.g. no periods, they like big breasts)
- Male/female relationships, experience (e.g. Jura has no concept of birth control)
- any flight/space travel/combat experience or technology unique to your character's setting
- beauty, fashion, and body image
- pregnancy/marriage/family
- diet/exercise/combat training, especially swordplay
- info about Earth, what it's like to live there
- positive F/F relationships/interest
- general questions about Mejare, her rank, ship, crew, etc. (anything that lets her brag about herself)
- compliments

Bad/Overdone Topics

- "How do two women make babies?" Cell/gene splicing. Normal pregnancy.
- "Your sword/dress/clothes/guns are so advanced!" Not really.
- "omg u r an alien" She's a human.
- Don't treat her like a loredump machine. Ask something that your character would have an opinion on the answer to.
- her past (very little is known, and some side material is untranslated, so I'd rather not make anything up)

Barnette

- Jura is accompanied by her girlfriend, Barnette Orangello [bar-NET OH-ren-JEH-lo, バーネット・オランジェロ]. Barnette is a fellow pilot on Jura's subteam (sometimes leading her own) and also helps manage the ship's weapon stock and delivery system ("Regisystem"). She is aggressive, irritable, and unsociable, as well as rather humorless and unwilling to play cards. (She also doesn't know how.) She spends the game patrolling the surroundings, but occasionally appears to react to something or speak to Jura. You can target her directly if you wish.
- They don't always share interests, but Jura and Barnette are attached at the hip and haunt the ship's halls together. Just as Jura often relies on Barnette to take charge in combat, Barnette usually defers to Jura for socializing.
- Barnette likes to collect antique guns---that is to say, modern guns. Her personal favorite sidearm is her CZ 75 pistol, but she also owns a variety of heavier weapons and looks for any excuse to bust them out. Weapon storage was her family's business before she was forced into piracy.
- She is also a talented cook and frequently bakes cakes and sweets, having taken care of multiple sisters growing up. Between the two of them, Barnette is generally more independent, and Jura more clingy.
- Despite sometimes feeling exasperated by Jura's schemes and antics, Barnette is also genuinely in love and can just as easily fangirl over her. She often captures Jura's beauty and showmanship on film, at Jura's behest, and she wants to be the Oma (egg donator) to Jura's baby.
- Barnette seems to have little interest in men and once gained a reputation for being particularly harsh towards their prisoners. But if Jura is fascinated by something, it doesn't take much to get her to follow along.
- Barnette's stated age is 18 in side material, but the implied timeline of the series puts her at 19 here. Her birthday is October 4th.
- Instead of masturbating, Jura calls upon Barnette to have sex with her, and responds in kind. Barnette cums before Jura does, 20 ticks in. While they don't completely ignore everyone else, their pillow talk is extremely lovey-dovey and melodramatic. (In general, feel free to target how obnoxious the two of them can be, even earlier on.)
- After finishing, Jura puts her boots back on and then briefly falls asleep with Barnette.

Misc.

- Any character capable of sensing supernatural or psychic power should detect a faint aura around Jura, enough to raise an eyebrow. This is because:
- Jura pilots a transformed Dread (gunship) and a super robot fusion mech called a Vandread. Both are the result of contact with their main ship's "Paksis" (PAKE-sis) energy core.
- The Paksis is otherworldly and also granted Jura a mild psychic link with some of her crewmates who shared the experience. Their transformed ships draw power from this sort of spiritual energy (ki) that the pilots put out.
- Jura prefers a defensive, supportive approach to combat. This is reflected in her Vandread's shielding capabilities.
- ON STAGE 4, Jura puts on a big show of stripping her dress/biggest clothing item in alts, showing most of her nude body all at once and getting Barnette to film her. Not only does a camera become present, but this preoccupies her from making any detailed conversation. Keep topics simple/focused on her.
- By her final stages, Jura does a lot of posing and sometimes teases others with her breasts. Official material tends to suggest that she is the "boobs" to Meia's "butt." She still has a lot of butt poses because that's what I like.

For more, see her Situations, Collectibles, and Markers.
